_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MIXED, and it is the FOLIAGE TILE of the bottom row -- the best leaf material found in z1lower by a wide margin. The right third is a great VINE-DRAPED TREE: ochre rope-like limbs across the top with long pendant tendrils of blue-green trifoliate leaves hanging straight down like a curtain, over the heads of two standing women. That blue-green is unmistakable and there is nothing else like it in this row. The left two thirds is the moving household on an ochre road -- a porter, a driver leading an OX, and a woman with a child riding it -- against a cliff of hemp-fibre rock. Below the road, a bank of rounded boulders and the river. So: foliage right, figures centre-left, rock and water below. The one dangerous look-alike is the cliff behind the party, whose ridges are capped with dark round 苔點 moss dots -- dark, repeated, clustered, and completely without the blue-green wash that marks every real leaf in this tile. Colour is the reliable separator here, in this tile only, because the leaves are washed and the rock is not.

objects.name: the left curtain of hanging vine leaves
objects.note: PRIME FOLIAGE. Long pendant tendrils falling from above the top edge, each strung with paired blue-green ovate leaves, hanging clear of everything behind them against bare silk. This is the easiest hinge subject in the whole bottom row: the tendrils are already vertical, well separated, and read correctly under a pendulum swing from a hinge at the top edge. Do NOT swing them as a block -- they are individual strands and should lag one another

objects.name: hanging vine sprays over the standing woman's head
objects.note: same vine, the band that passes directly above and beside the woman with the fan. Her head and hair ornament sit INSIDE the lower part of this box -- the box is unavoidable here because the leaves surround her, so any mask built from it must exclude the figure or her face will deform

objects.name: the dense vine-and-branch tangle at the top right
objects.note: leaves and ochre rope-vine STEMS are interwoven at 1:1 here and cannot be separated by a box. Read at 3x: the blue-green trifoliate clusters are leaves, the pale ochre ropes threading between them are woody vine and must not stretch. Hinge this box from its top edge with a small amplitude so the ropes read as swaying, not as rubber

objects.name: pendant leaf sprays down the right edge, behind the standing attendant
objects.note: the lower reach of the same curtain, clipped by the right edge -- it continues into t002, so match phase there or the seam will flicker

objects.name: leafy shrub arching up from the rock shelf, lower right
objects.note: a SEPARATE plant from the vine above it -- a low bramble whose thin stems arch up off the boulder shelf carrying clusters of small blue-green leaves. Small but unmistakable, and the kind of leaf mass that gets missed and then sits frozen next to a moving canopy. Hinge at the base of the stems, not the top: this one grows up, so it bends rather than swings

objects.name: the heavy ochre limbs and dark trunk crossing the top right
objects.note: the woody armature the whole vine curtain hangs from -- thick pale-ochre limbs with a dark ink trunk behind, clipped by the top edge. RIGID. It overlaps vine-tangle-right on purpose: this box records what inside that box must not move, so a leaf mask built from the tree boxes should subtract the thickest limbs here

objects.name: the ox carrying the woman and child
objects.note: an ANIMAL (kind 'figure' because the enum has no animal) -- tan body, horned head turned to the left, led on a rope. The compositional centre of the tile. Motion 'none': a rigid cel. A partial walk cycle on a horned ox reads as broken immediately

objects.name: woman riding the ox with a small child in her arms
objects.note: the emotional centre of 移居 -- the family being moved. Two faces at close range in a small box; NOTHING above the shoulders may deform. The blue-grey skirt falling down the ox's flank is the only part that should move

objects.name: man leading the ox with a rope, holding a whip
objects.note: a gourd hangs at his waist; the lead rope runs from his hand to the ox's muzzle. If the robe swings, the rope must stay attached at both ends -- it is the one line in this tile that ties two moving objects together

objects.name: porter walking right with a rolled bundle on his back
objects.note: SAME MAN as 'porter-with-bundle-right' in t000 -- the tiles overlap by 264 master px and he appears in both. Animate him once, in one tile, or he will move out of phase with himself across the seam

objects.name: standing woman holding a fan, under the vine
objects.note: the finest face in the tile -- red lip, black coiffure with a red ornament. She stands INSIDE the vine curtain, so she must be cut out of any foliage mask before it is used. Long hem, wide sleeves: good robe motion, zero tolerance on the head

objects.name: attendant with a basket at the right edge
objects.note: clipped by the right edge and continuing into t002; carries a small covered basket. Also stands inside the vine box

objects.name: the cliff wall rising behind the household
objects.note: 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes with dark moss dots strung along every ridge. THE LOOK-ALIKE IN THIS TILE: those dot chains are round, repeated and clustered exactly like the vine leaves opposite -- and they carry no wash at all. In this tile colour settles it. Never animate

objects.name: the moss-dotted lip of the bridge deck at the left edge
objects.note: the far end of t000's trestle bridge arriving in the overlap strip -- a chain of heavy round dots along a ruled edge. Rigid. Not a hedge, though it reads as one at a glance

objects.name: the ochre road the household is walking on
objects.note: a broad pale-yellow sweep of ground, the plane every figure and the ox stands on -- share their depth with it or the party will slide off the road. The ochre wash here is the same yellow that autumn foliage carries elsewhere in the scroll; it is dirt

objects.name: the bank of rounded boulders below the road
objects.note: big soft-shouldered stones in raking hemp-fibre strokes, dark moss dots along the tops. Never animate

objects.name: dark rock at the bottom left, at the water's edge
objects.note: clipped by the left edge; ripple lines break against its foot

objects.name: the rock shelf on the right that the shrub grows out of
objects.note: overlaps shrub-on-rock-lower-right deliberately -- this box is the STONE and that box is the plant standing on it. A mask that takes this whole region as foliage is the exact rejected failure

objects.name: dark angular outcrop at the bottom right corner
objects.note: clipped by the right and bottom edges. Heavily inked and slightly roof-like in silhouette, but there is no ruled line anywhere in it -- it is stone

objects.name: the river across the bottom of the tile
objects.note: bare silk with long horizontal ripple lines; the same water as t000's river, one tile downstream. Move it as one surface across both tiles or the seam will shear

objects.name: fine grass or reed strokes at the bottom edge
objects.note: HONESTLY UNRESOLVED, and small. Thin springing strokes rising out of the water at the very bottom edge -- grass or reeds, not tree leaves, so leavesVisible is false and it stays out of the canopy mask. Only about 35 px of the tuft is inside this tile; the rest is in t005, which is where the call should actually be made
